text:
The new Redis 8.10 server on port 6380 now holds an exact copy of the production data and runs as a standalone primary that accepts writes.

**How I copied it:** I made the new server a temporary replica of the old one (`REPLICAOF 127.0.0.1 6379`). It did a full sync and loaded the 7.2 snapshot with all 3,270 keys and none expired. Once it had fully caught up, I turned replication off (`REPLICAOF NO ONE`), so it went back to being a primary. Replication was only switched on at runtime and never written to `/etc/redis/redis.conf`, so the server will still come up as a primary after a restart. I also saved a snapshot to disk on the new server (`BGSAVE`), so the data survives a restart.

**Check:** a script compared all 16 databases on both servers, key by key, and found 0 differences across the 3,270 keys. It checked:
- **Keys:** the same keys in every database (db0: 2,920 keys, 900 with a time to live; db2: 350 keys, 150 with a time to live).
- **Types and values:** the same type and value for every string, hash, list, set, sorted set and stream.
- **Time to live:** the same remaining time on each key, within 5 seconds (the gap is just the time the check took to run).
- **Streams:** the same entries and last ID, and the same consumer groups, including each group's position, consumers and pending messages.

**Writes:** to confirm the new server accepts writes, I briefly wrote and then deleted one test key in the empty db15, so no data was left behind.

The old 7.2 server is still running as a primary with its data unchanged. Its only replica connection was the new server's, which is now gone. Both servers allow local connections without a password, the same as before.
